rows.diagnosis: ADJACENT: vitiligo ('stable or segmental vitiligo' in Methods; abstract: 'stable vitiligo not responding to medical line of treatment'); [not IGH]; Module 5-damage-repair lead (graft transplantation precedent)
rows.design: retrospective single-centre case series, all patients who underwent SBEG January 2008 to December 2013; no comparator; recall visit December 2013
rows.body_site: not reported per patient (Results mention face, lips and limbs; donor site outer thigh in 22 patients, inner arm in 8)
rows.skin_tone: not reported [single centre in Kerala, India]
rows.patients_evaluable: 30 in Table 1 [26 re-examined in December 2013; for the 4 who did not respond the last visit's records and photographs were used]
rows.analysis_unit: patient (Tables give 'number of patients'; [how a grade was assigned to a patient with more than one grafted lesion is not reported])
rows.intervention: suction blister epidermal grafting (SBEG), day care, local anaesthesia; patients 'not advised specifically to take phototherapy after the procedure'
rows.time_from_start: 2 to 62 months follow-up (mean 23.6, SD 17.79) [counted from the SBEG procedure; per-patient times not reported]
rows.time_from_last_treatment: NOT_DERIVABLE: follow-up of 2 to 62 months (mean 23.6) is given as one range for the whole series, not per patient or per grade; the number of SBEG sessions per patient and any later treatment are not reported ('not advised specifically to take phototherapy' does not say none was taken, and Discussion says 'even without postgraft phototherapy', [suggesting some patients had it])
rows.complete_match: not reported (no colour-match grade, count or scale). The source's colour statements are all qualitative: Results, 'The face and lips showed an excellent result, color match and persistent pigment retention'; Figure 2 caption, lower-lip vitiligo 'fully repigmented and normalized after surgery'; Figure 3 caption, 'A near total re-pigmentation with excellent color match' (segmental vitiligo of the face); Discussion, 'Color and texture match with the surrounding skin is generally good' [a general statement citing reference 6, not a result of this study]
rows.dark_overshoot: not reported for the recipient site (the source reports postinflammatory hyperpigmentation for the donor site, see texture_or_scar; it does not describe recipient-site hyperpigmentation)
rows.texture_or_scar: donor site: completely healed 16 of 30 patients (53.3%), mild postinflammatory hyperpigmentation 12 (40.0%), significant postinflammatory hyperpigmentation 2 (6.7%); 'no keloids or hypertrophic scars in any of the patients' [donor site; recipient-site texture not reported]
rows.attrition: 4 of 30 did not attend the December 2013 recall; their last recorded visit and photographs were used [so their follow-up time is shorter than the recall date implies]
rows.citation: Ashique KT, Kaliyadan F. Long-Term Follow-up and Donor Site Changes Evaluation in Suction Blister Epidermal Grafting Done for Stable Vitiligo: A Retrospective Study. Indian J Dermatol 2015;60(4):369-72
rows.endpoint_definition: share of patients whose treated area was graded excellent (95-100% repigmentation) by doctor observation at the last follow-up [variable time per patient]
rows.assessment_method: doctor observation of percentage repigmentation of the treated area, four grades (Methods: excellent 95-100%, good 65-94%, fair 25-64%, poor 0-24%), with patient questionnaire and photographs at each visit; [blinding and assessor identity not reported]
rows.arm_result: 15 of 30 patients (50.0%) graded excellent, 95-100% repigmentation of the treated area
rows.patient_noticeability: not reported per grade (patient satisfaction for all 30: very happy 16 (53.3%), happy 8 (26.7%), satisfactory 3 (10.0%), unhappy 3 (10.0%); correlation with doctor grade Spearman's rho 0.866)
rows.uncertainty: Diagnosis: [not an IGH study]; vitiligo, a Module 5-damage-repair lead (epidermal graft transplantation with long but variable follow-up) entered at Gate A; it says nothing directly about IGH spots. [Module 5-damage-repair is not an allowed module in tools/ledger.py, so the row is filed under 1-hypopigmentation with an ADJACENT diagnosis.] Retrospective case series, no control arm, 30 patients, small sample and variable follow-up named by the authors as the main limitation. Follow-up 2 to 62 months is reported only for the whole series, never per grade or per patient, so no grade can be tied to a time point and months after final treatment is NOT_DERIVABLE; number of SBEG sessions per patient and any later treatment are not reported. Grade cut-offs differ between abstract ('fair (24-64%), good (64-94)') and Methods ('good with 65-94%, fair with 25-64%'); Table 1 uses 25-64% and 65-94%. Abstract says grades were assigned 'depending on the patient satisfaction', while Methods and Table 1 say doctor observation of the treated area; patient satisfaction is reported separately in Table 2. Grades are percentage repigmentation of the treated area estimated by doctor observation; blinding and instrument not reported; photographs were taken at every visit but [whether grades were read from photographs is not reported]; [assessor identity not reported]. An 'excellent' grade (95-100%) is partial repigmentation, not complete area coverage and not a colour match. Unit is the patient; number of grafted lesions per patient and how one grade was given to a patient with several lesions are not reported. Body sites per patient not reported; text says face and lips did best and limbs worse, with no counts. Colour match is described qualitatively, with no count, scale or time point, in the Results sentence on face and lips ('excellent result, color match and persistent pigment retention') and in the Figure 2 ('fully repigmented and normalized after surgery') and Figure 3 ('near total re-pigmentation with excellent color match') captions, each showing one face or lip case. Post-graft phototherapy: Methods say patients 'were not advised specifically to take phototherapy after the procedure', but Discussion says 'Many of our patients showed very good results post-SBEG even without postgraft phototherapy' [which suggests some patients may have had postgraft phototherapy; who and when are not reported]. 4 of 30 patients did not attend the December 2013 recall; their last recorded visit was used, so their follow-up is shorter than the series range implies [and their grades may be at an earlier time]. Diagnosis wording differs: Methods 'stable or segmental vitiligo', abstract 'stable vitiligo not responding to medical line of treatment'. Statistics contain an impossible value: 'Spearman's rho 0.482, P = -0.007' for site vs donor area changes. Follow-up 2 to 62 months is reported only for the whole series, never per grade or per patient, so no grade can be tied to a time point and months after final treatment is NOT_DERIVABLE; number of SBEG sessions per patient and any later treatment are not reported. Grade cut-offs differ between abstract ('fair (24-64%), good (64-94)') and Methods ('good with 65-94%, fair with 25-64%'); Table 1 uses 25-64% and 65-94%. Abstract says grades were assigned 'depending on the patient satisfaction', while Methods and Table 1 say doctor observation of the treated area; patient satisfaction is reported separately in Table 2. Grades are percentage repigmentation of the treated area estimated by doctor observation; blinding and instrument not reported; photographs were taken at every visit but [whether grades were read from photographs is not reported]; [assessor identity not reported]. An 'excellent' grade (95-100%) is partial repigmentation, not complete area coverage and not a colour match. Unit is the patient; number of grafted lesions per patient and how one grade was given to a patient with several lesions are not reported. Body sites per patient not reported; text says face and lips did best and limbs worse, with no counts. Colour match is described qualitatively, with no count, scale or time point, in the Results sentence on face and lips ('excellent result, color match and persistent pigment retention') and in the Figure 2 ('fully repigmented and normalized after surgery') and Figure 3 ('near total re-pigmentation with excellent color match') captions, each showing one face or lip case. Post-graft phototherapy: Methods say patients 'were not advised specifically to take phototherapy after the procedure', but Discussion says 'Many of our patients showed very good results post-SBEG even without postgraft phototherapy' [which suggests some patients may have had postgraft phototherapy; who and when are not reported]. 4 of 30 patients did not attend the December 2013 recall; their last recorded visit was used, so their follow-up is shorter than the series range implies [and their grades may be at an earlier time]. Diagnosis wording differs: Methods 'stable or segmental vitiligo', abstract 'stable vitiligo not responding to medical line of treatment'. Statistics contain an impossible value: 'Spearman's rho 0.482, P = -0.007' for site vs donor area changes. Tables 1-3 are published only as images; their cells were transcribed into the excerpt (image URLs in the excerpt) and should be checked against the images. This row is patient satisfaction, not a repigmentation or colour measure; it does not say whether the spot is still noticeable.

rows.intervention: suction blister epidermal grafting (SBEG), day care, local anaesthesia; patients 'not advised specifically to take phototherapy after the procedure'
rows.time_from_start: 2 to 62 months follow-up (mean 23.6, SD 17.79) [counted from the SBEG procedure; per-patient times not reported]
rows.time_from_last_treatment: NOT_DERIVABLE: follow-up of 2 to 62 months (mean 23.6) is given as one range for the whole series, not per patient or per grade; the number of SBEG sessions per patient and any later treatment are not reported ('not advised specifically to take phototherapy' does not say none was taken, and Discussion says 'even without postgraft phototherapy', [suggesting some patients had it])
rows.complete_match: not reported (no colour-match grade, count or scale). The source's colour statements are all qualitative: Results, 'The face and lips showed an excellent result, color match and persistent pigment retention'; Figure 2 caption, lower-lip vitiligo 'fully repigmented and normalized after surgery'; Figure 3 caption, 'A near total re-pigmentation with excellent color match' (segmental vitiligo of the face); Discussion, 'Color and texture match with the surrounding skin is generally good' [a general statement citing reference 6, not a result of this study]
rows.dark_overshoot: not reported for the recipient site (the source reports postinflammatory hyperpigmentation for the donor site, see texture_or_scar; it does not describe recipient-site hyperpigmentation)
rows.texture_or_scar: donor site: completely healed 16 of 30 patients (53.3%), mild postinflammatory hyperpigmentation 12 (40.0%), significant postinflammatory hyperpigmentation 2 (6.7%); 'no keloids or hypertrophic scars in any of the patients' [donor site; recipient-site texture not reported]
rows.attrition: 4 of 30 did not attend the December 2013 recall; their last recorded visit and photographs were used [so their follow-up time is shorter than the recall date implies]

Thirty patients (21 females and 9 males) with stable or segmental vitiligo were inducted into the study.
All the patients who underwent SBEG in our department during the period from January 2008 to December 2013 were included in the study.
The donor area was the outer aspect of the thigh in 22 patients and inner aspect of the arm in 8 patients.
